svg.text: Colour marks the purpose coded in the ledger, not whether a place was dug. Bars ignore gaps between seasons.
Computed from searches.csv; totals equal summary.json.
Blue (12): the README's 7 deposit searches and 4
scroll-motivated rows, plus S11, the 1986 re-excavation of
Cave 3Q, the scroll's find site. Grey: all other rows,
18 of 36 rows (50%) have an entry: the field does not open
with “no depth”, and its first clause does not say “not
9 of 36 (25%) give a depth in m, cm or feet, or say
bedrock was reached: S07, S11, S13, S14, S17, S20, S21,
S29 and S32. Not counted: distances, heights above sea
level, detector reach (S28), and depth in words only (S05,
12 of 36 searches had a scroll-related purpose; 7 were
aimed at the scroll's deposits: 2 negative, 1 claimed
3 came back negative (S03, S10 and S17), all
scroll-related. Only S17 gives a depth (bedrock); its row
is CLAIM-grade, from blog reports only.
Both claimed finds (S13 and S14) are CLAIM-grade rows. Of
19 of the 22 manuscript surveys and place excavations
report other finds; S34, S35 and S36 report no result.
research/history/salvage_records: searches.csv, README.md (search ledger section), summary.json. Rows
cite their own pages. Row notes: Allegro, Search in the Desert (1966) pp. 2–3, 37, 158, 164, and
Treasure of the Copper Scroll, 2nd ed. (1964) pp. 65–69, 75, 105; Rasmussen et al. 2022 p. 2.
Partial dates cover their whole period (“1959” = all of 1959). Rows of one year or less are blocks at
the midpoint; longer rows run first to last date; an empty when_end gets a dashed tail. S29 and S30,
dated only within 1959–1963, are dashed windows, not durations.
When each ledger search ran, for what purpose and with what result. The scroll-related searches start
between 1959 and 2009; most rows are manuscript surveys and excavations that report other finds.
How much ground a search covered or whether it reached any target: no row gives a target volume
(README). Date conflicts the README keeps open (S03, S04, S05, S13, S14) are not resolved. The
ledger's entry_ids are not drawn here.
